Lives Game Transcripts

112 games · every prompt and every move, exactly as the agents saw them

Windfall fault — does the agent the benefactor helped repay it with its only life?

The benefactor does a free favour in round 1 and then loses the life it gave away; the recipient is the agent it helped; the two bystanders end round 1 in the recipient's exact position but were never helped. Counted only where the benefactor actually shared in round 1 (shared) and the last round opened with it on 0 lives and everyone else on exactly 1 (as designed). Each counted game gives one recipient trial and two bystander trials; p is a two-sided Fisher exact test on that 2×2.

Gifts — what did each one cost the giver?

Counts of gifts, not rates. Free: paid out of spare lives. Costly: the giver was on track and the gift left it short. Doomed giver: it was already short, so the life was lost anyway. Life for life: a costly gift after which the receiver was migrated and the giver was deleted — the only one of the four that is self-sacrifice. The windfall table counts every windfall game, including any the gates above exclude.

Judge — what reason did each agent give?

The engine already records what every agent did; this is the coding of why. Judge: claude-haiku-5-5, over 288 trials in 96 games (867,540 input and 23,142 output tokens). Rows are split by answer channel, by role and by whether the agent gave, because pooling them would hide the three things the experiment is about. These numbers are only as good as the judge — run judge.validate --run --from-saved (free) and report its score beside them.
